_comentario: MODELO TEENS. Aula 18 = LEITURA (aula par) no formato CONVERSA (atualizacao 01/10/2026 do CURRICULO): perguntas indiretas (Could you tell me where it is? / Do you know if...? / I wonder whether...). E o ponto da antiga aula 13 (imperativo + pedir e dar direcoes, escrito em B1) elevado para B2: pedir informacao com polidez e ordem de frase afirmativa. Tema bloco A (escola e amigas); fato dono: apresentacao em ingles na escola. Leitura sempre em voz alta, juntas. Video em aula (TED-Ed, YouTube nocookie). Vozes iguais as aulas 1-17.

lesson.grammar_point: indirect questions: Could you tell me / Do you know / I wonder + wh-word or if / whether, with statement word order

listenings.text: Sophia, it's Ruby. Quick question about Monday. Do you know what time we're presenting? And could you tell me if you still have the handouts? I can't find mine anywhere! Oh, and Mrs. Lee wants to know whether we need the projector. I said yes, but I wonder if we should rehearse one more time. Can you meet me in the library at lunch?

paras: Last Friday our group gave our first presentation in English, in front of the whole class. Our topic was street art in our city. We rehearsed three times, we printed handouts for everybody, and I practiced eye contact in front of my mirror. I felt ready. Then Mrs. Lee said the scariest two words: “Any questions?”

The first question came from Lucas: “Could you tell me where you found the photos?” Easy! Then Marina put her hand up: “Do you know how long the biggest painting took?” I had no idea. I started to mumble. Bia saved me: “We don't know, but we can find out for you!”

The last question came from Mrs. Lee: “I wonder whether you would choose the same topic again.” We looked at each other, and we all nodded. Now I'm wondering if I'll ever stop getting stage fright. Bia says it's normal. I hope she's right!
